sources.entry: dayGLANCE - Day planner with drag-and-drop time blocking, inbox, recurring tasks, habits, routines, goals, projects and Pomodoro focus mode, plus iCal and CalDAV calendar sync. Data stays in the browser, with optional WebDAV or GLANCEvault sync. (Source Code, Clients) MIT Javascript/Docker

summary.one_liner: A privacy-first, browser-based day planner with drag-and-drop time-blocking, an inbox, recurring tasks, habits, goals and projects, and optional self-hosting via Docker or WebDAV/Nextcloud sync.
summary.what_it_does: dayGLANCE is a day planner that puts tasks and calendar events on a 24-hour timeline you can drag and resize, with data kept in the browser by default. It includes a smart inbox with priorities and #tag filtering, recurring tasks, routines that populate a day from templates, habit tracking, and a Pomodoro-style Focus Mode. Goals, projects and optional hyperGLANCE project sessions are available in a separate section that must be enabled in settings. Sync is optional: WebDAV/Nextcloud, direct access to a synced folder, GLANCEvault, and iCloud on Apple platforms, with optional end-to-end encryption. iCal/CalDAV calendars can be imported, and an Obsidian vault can be synced directly or through an optional Bridge plugin.
use_cases: sync tasks across devices via Nextcloud or WebDAV
import iCal or CalDAV calendars into a daily timeline
sync tasks and daily notes with an Obsidian vault
show the day on an e-ink or wall display
how_to_run: Try it without installing at dayglance.app
Create a docker-compose.yml with image ghcr.io/krelltunez/dayglance:latest mapping port 6767:80
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd dayglance, npm install
npm run dev (development) or npm run build (production)
notable: Data stays in the browser; nothing is sent to a server unless the user enables sync
Docker image built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, including Raspberry Pi
Built-in proxy for WebDAV and calendar feeds that lack CORS headers, with an option to block private network targets
Optional AES-256-GCM end-to-end encryption for sync data
Obsidian integration works without a plugin, with an optional Bridge plugin for agenda and task sources
caveats: Browser sync file size limit is 4.5 MB on dayglance.app and 50 MB in the Docker image
Stream Deck plugin requires the desktop app installed on the same system
Some features (JOBO) are marked experimental and off by default; AI, health and other add-ons are opt-in
Docker proxy should not be exposed publicly without authentication or a reverse proxy
keywords: keep my tasks on my own server
